submissions.findingTextShort: The current Vyleesi label establishes a narrow approved bremelanotide product/indication and must be kept separate from gray-market PT-141 products.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current DailyMed Vyleesi label, revised March 2024, defines the approved bremelanotide product and its narrow indication, contraindications and clinically important warnings. The labeled contraindications are uncontrolled hypertension or known cardiovascular disease; pregnancy is handled under use-in-specific-populations/fetal-harm counseling rather than as a formal contraindication. Approved Vyleesi identity must remain separate from unapproved or research-use products marketed as PT-141, and label facts require dated regulatory freshness rather than a generic peptide-supplement status.
submissions.populationContext: Regulatory labeling for the approved Vyleesi/bremelanotide product and indicated premenopausal HSDD population.
submissions.usageContext: Approved bremelanotide/Vyleesi product; not interchangeable with gray-market PT-141 formulations.
submissions.safetyContext: Label-defined cardiovascular contraindications, BP/HR effects, hyperpigmentation, nausea, oral-drug interactions and pregnancy counseling require exact product/regulatory scope.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Regulatory status and labeling can change; preserve label revision date and do not transfer approval to unapproved PT-141 products.

submissions.findingTextShort: Two randomized Phase 3 RECONNECT trials found statistically significant but modest desire/distress improvements with bremelanotide in premenopausal women with HSDD.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Two randomized Phase 3 RECONNECT trials evaluated bremelanotide in premenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder and reported statistically significant but modest improvements in sexual desire and related distress. These are disease/indication-specific data for the studied bremelanotide formulation and cannot be generalized to male sexual performance, bodybuilding, generic libido enhancement or unapproved PT-141 products.
submissions.populationContext: Premenopausal women with acquired generalized HSDD represented in two randomized Phase 3 trials.
submissions.usageContext: Bremelanotide in the approved-product development context; indication-specific efficacy.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Effect magnitude is modest and indication-specific; do not transfer to other populations or gray-market formulations.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 52-week open-label extension provides longer-duration tolerability context for bremelanotide but is not a randomized efficacy substitute.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 52-week open-label extension of the bremelanotide program provides longer-duration exposure and tolerability context. Because it is open-label, it should not substitute for randomized efficacy evidence and cannot establish safety for unapproved formulations or populations outside the studied HSDD program. Adverse effects and discontinuation context should remain product- and population-specific.
submissions.populationContext: Longer-term extension participants from the bremelanotide HSDD clinical-development program.
submissions.usageContext: Open-label longer-duration bremelanotide exposure; tolerability context rather than comparative efficacy.
submissions.safetyContext: Longer-duration clinical exposure receipt for the studied product; not comprehensive lifetime or cross-formulation safety proof.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Open-label design and selected continuation population constrain inference.

submissions.findingTextShort: An older randomized trial in sildenafil nonresponders with erectile dysfunction is historical male off-label evidence, not part of the approved HSDD indication.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: An older randomized study evaluated bremelanotide in men with erectile dysfunction who were sildenafil nonresponders. This is historical off-label male evidence and must remain separate from the approved premenopausal-female HSDD indication. It cannot be used to imply general male enhancement, current regulatory approval for ED, or equivalence of gray-market PT-141 products.
submissions.populationContext: Men with erectile dysfunction who were sildenafil nonresponders in an older randomized study.
submissions.usageContext: Historical off-label male bremelanotide research; not an approved indication.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Historical trial context and off-label population prevent regulatory or broad consumer generalization.
